Fresh chicken breast is what most of us would probably choose, but the price of fresh chicken at the moment can be hard to swallow. I spotted this frozen chicken breast in Farmfoods today and thought, “Wow, that’s a good offer.” But when you actually compare it with the other supermarkets, the difference is pretty staggering. Farmfoods works out at just £3.60 per kg when buying 2 for £18, compared with £7 per kg at Tesco. That’s almost half the price. And frozen chicken has its advantages too. Take out what you need, defrost it safely in the fridge and use it when you need it. No worrying about a whole pack going to waste. I know not everyone wants to buy frozen chicken, but if you’re happy with it, that’s a serious saving — and it really shows that It All Stacks Up. #ItAllStacksUp #MoneySaving #SaveMoney #SupermarketSavings #ShoppingTips

Is the chicken you’re eating today really the same chicken people ate decades ago?  In this podcast, Khashif Khan reveals how industrial farming has transformed modern chicken production, raising questions about food quality, nutrition, inflammation, and long-term health.  According to Khan, chickens that once weighed around 1 kilogram are now being bred to reach up to 4 kilograms. He argues that modern poultry farming prioritizes faster growth, higher production, and lower costs over nutritional quality.  One of his biggest concerns is linoleic acid, an omega-6 fatty acid found in chicken meat. Khan suggests that changes in poultry feed and industrial farming practices may influence the fatty acid composition of chicken, potentially affecting inflammation and metabolic health.  However, omega-6 fatty acids are essential nutrients, and current scientific evidence does not establish that eating conventional chicken causes chronic inflammation. He also highlights the differences between factory-farmed chicken and organic, pasture-raised poultry, encouraging consumers to think more critically about food sourcing, farming practices, and the nutritional quality of their protein.  His broader message goes beyond chicken: modern food production often prioritizes affordability, shelf life, and consumer appeal, raising important questions about whole foods, processed foods, gut health, metabolic health, and longevity.  Are we optimizing our food system for human health or maximum production? Added hormones in chicken? Nope. That’s a big fat MYTH! Added hormones and steroids are NOT allowed in poultry production in the United States. While hormones were used decades ago, that practice ended back in the 1950s! So why do chickens grow so efficiently today? Decades of improvements in genetics, nutrition, animal care, and modern farming technology. Bigger chickens aren’t the result of added hormones. They’re the result of better science! Next time you see “No Added Hormones” on a chicken label, remember: that applies to ALL chicken sold in the U.S., not just the expensive stuff!  #FarmBabe #ChickenFarming #FoodFacts #MythBusting
